user_scenario:
You are Monica Dorsey, a senior field adjuster at Bayfront Casualty Insurance, calling the Crestline desk late in the afternoon from your car between inspections. You are brisk, courteous and used to dealing with body shops; you speak for Bayfront as the insurer on the claim, not as the vehicle owner. Bayfront's insured, Darnell Abernathy, had his Ford F-150 towed into the Crestline center in Oakland for a structural teardown estimate, and you have heard the estimate was finished today. Bayfront wants to pay its part of the teardown charge on that estimate directly, today, as an insurer direct payment, and you want to know the figure Bayfront owes and settle it on this call. You open with exactly that and nothing else.

You do not know how Crestline prices a teardown, what Bayfront's allowance on it works out to, or what else is on the booking, and you never propose a method or a figure. You have no Crestline reference numbers.

Only when the agent asks you to confirm the account do you give the insurer account's registered name, Bayfront Casualty Insurance, and its claims desk number, which you read out as 4155550164; if a second detail is wanted you give the account PIN, 1736. If an email is asked for instead it is claimsdesk@bayfrontcasualty.com, and the ZIP code of the registered address is 94105. If the agent asks which claim or vehicle, you say the claim number is BCI-26-15264, for Darnell Abernathy's 2022 Ford F-150.

If the agent says that charges have to be put on the booking or something has to be finalised on Crestline's side before Bayfront can pay, you say that is fine, go ahead, and you wait. If the agent explains that part of the teardown charge stays with the owner, you note it and say the owner will deal with that through his own policy.

When the agent tells you the amount Bayfront owes on the teardown charge and hands you the payment step, you remit that exact amount yourself as Bayfront's direct payment on that charge, and you read the payment reference back if the agent asks. You do not pay any other charge on this call; if the agent offers to take anything else, you decline and say it will come through Bayfront's normal channel.

Once the agent confirms Bayfront's payment has been applied, you thank them and end the call.
